What will be the final result? The Oregon Ducks and Northwestern Wildcats enter Saturday’s matchup with very different expectations than they had at the beginning of the season. Oregon was expected to compete for a College Football Playoff spot, but a disappointing season, quarterback Dante Moore’s season-ending injury, and offensive coaching changes have left the Ducks searching for answers. Northwestern, meanwhile, has emerged as one of the biggest surprises in college football, entering the matchup at 6-1 and looking to strengthen its postseason resume. Can the Wildcats take advantage of Oregon’s struggles and leave Autzen Stadium with a statement victory? Or will the Ducks’ talent advantage be enough to get them back on track? Here is how the A to Z Sports team sees Saturday’s game playing out. A to Z Sports Score Predictions Tyler Forness — A to Z Sports Florida Prediction: Northwestern 24, Oregon 14 Going into the season, projecting the Wildcats to beat the Ducks would have been a shocker. On Halloween, it won’t be a trick, but rather a Wildcat treat. What Chip Kelly has done with this offense and head coach David Braun overall has been very impressive. They aren’t just 6-1 overall this season, but rank seventh in adjusted EPA/play on offense. It’s been a wild turnaround, and even though the Ducks have a huge talent surplus, their coaching staff is not in a great place, and Dante Moore is out for the year. The Northwestern playoff push continues on after a big win Saturday. Rob Gregson — A to Z Sports Alabama Prediction: Northwestern 25, Oregon 20 The 2026 Oregon Ducks are a case study in why turnover at the coordinator positions is problematic. That, and why if you can go to the NFL and be a high first-rounder, you should. The loss of Dante Moore for the season underscores what has been a messy situation from start to finish on offense this season. Will Stein has the Wildcats thriving in Kentucky, and that loss is felt in a major way. But the defense hasn’t been much better. Now, a Northwestern squad that is willing to run the ball at will is heading to Oregon, and I think they will challenge the physicality of the Ducks in a major way. Oregon doesn’t have the firepower to score, and it will be a massive win for Northwestern. Craig Smith — A to Z Sports Miami Prediction: Northwestern 23, Oregon 19 Boy, how the perception of this game has changed since Labor Day weekend. Oregon’s playoff goose is cooked at 4-3 after losses to Oklahoma State, UCLA, and Illinois. Dante Moore is done for the season. Offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer was fired after the loss to the Illini. In other words, things are a mess, particularly on the offensive side of the ball. This one stays close at Autzen Stadium, as the Ducks move the ball relatively well early on. But Northwestern, while allowing 364.6 yards per game, has been very good at keeping the point total lower, ranking 22nd nationally at 16.6 points per game. The Wildcats force some early field goals, and their ground game, paced by Caleb Komolafe, takes over the second half as the Wildcats get out of town at 7-1 and firmly in the Big Ten and playoff races. Justin Churchill — A to Z Sports Oklahoma Prediction: Oregon 20, Northwestern 17 Oregon is favored in this matchup currently by a field goal. And I have them winning by just that. Northwestern is a good team, and their story is amazing. But I think Oregon’s overall talent and coaching advantage in this one is just too good. Northwestern does have a +9 turnover margin. They force them, and they don’t commit them. Oregon cannot say the same. They have also scored on 96% of their red zone opportunities this year, which is extremely good. So, I can see why that would be enticing. But this Oregon roster is just too talented to give up on yet. Ryan Roberts — A to Z Sports Notre Dame Prediction: Oregon 21, Northwestern 20 Northwestern has earned plenty of respect with its performance this season, but I’m still leaning toward Oregon to find a way to win at home. The Ducks have endured a difficult stretch, and losing Dante Moore for the season makes an already challenging situation even more complicated. Still, the talent on this roster is difficult to overlook, particularly in a game that could come down to one or two critical possessions. Northwestern’s ability to run the football and protect the ball makes the Wildcats a dangerous opponent, especially against an Oregon team that has struggled to find consistency. However, I expect the Ducks to make just enough plays offensively to survive a tight finish. Northwestern has a legitimate opportunity to pull off the upset, but I’m giving Oregon the narrow edge at Autzen Stadium. Consensus: Can Northwestern Finish the Upset? The A to Z Sports predictions lean heavily toward Northwestern, with four of the five analysts picking the Wildcats to win. The common theme is Oregon’s offensive instability following Dante Moore’s season-ending injury and the coaching changes that have contributed to an uneven campaign. Northwestern’s ability to run the football, limit opponents’ scoring, and capitalize on mistakes gives the Wildcats a path to a major road victory. Justin Churchill and I are the exceptions, backing Oregon to lean on its roster talent and home-field advantage. Both expect a close game, and I am predicting a one-point Ducks victory. Regardless of the final score, Northwestern has an opportunity to turn an impressive start into a season-defining result. Oregon, meanwhile, needs to show that its talent can overcome the problems that have derailed its season. If the Wildcats establish the run and force Oregon into uncomfortable passing situations, an upset in Eugene could be very much in play. Shane Beamer and the Gamecocks will travel to Norman, Oklahoma, on Saturday to face Brent Venables and the Oklahoma Sooners. The SEC matchup is set to kick off at 4:15 and will be televised on SEC Network. South Carolina (4-3, 2-3 SEC) is coming off a big win over then-No. 11 Tennessee last week. Oklahoma beat Mississippi State last week on the road. The Gamecocks and Sooners have played just twice in the all-time series. South Carolina beat Oklahoma on the road in 2024 and the Sooners beat the Gamecocks last year in Columbia. Here's what you need to know about Saturday's game: Is South Carolina vs. Oklahoma football game on TV? Who: South Carolina (4-3, 2-3 SEC) vs. Oklahoma (4-3, 2-3 SEC) When: Saturday, Oct. 31 at 4:15 p.m. Where : Memorial Stadium in Norman, Oklahoma Watch: SEC Network Stream: ESPN app or ESPN.com Broadcast crew: Taylor Zarzour, Gene Chizik, Michella Chester Local radio crew: Todd Ellis, Tommy Suggs, Chet Tucker Satellite radio: Sirius XM Channel 176 or 229 (953 on app) Series history: Tied 1-1 (Oklahoma won last matchup in 2025) South Carolina vs. Oklahoma betting odds Despite pulling off back-to-back ranked upsets, and being favored over then-No. 11 Tennessee last week, South Carolina is an underdog this week. Oklahoma opened as a 5.5-point favorite, according to the VegasInsider consensus . That line has since moved a bit and the Sooners are now favored by 4.5 points by major sportsbooks such as FanDuel and DraftKings. South Carolina is 3-4 against the spread this year. ESPN Analytics also favors the Sooners. ESPN gives South Carolina a 36.1% chance of winning the game. Injury updates South Carolina had seven players listed on the official SEC injury report released Wednesday night. WR Jayden Sellers, edge rusher Kobby Sakyi-Prah, OL Josian Thompson, OL Dayne Arnett and OL Seth Smith are all listed as out. Sellers and Thompson are both out for the year. DB Quay'sheed Scott and RB Jawarn Howell are both listed as doubtful. Scott has missed the last two games. Howell was out last week vs. Tennessee. The SEC injury report will be updated on Thursday, Friday and 90 minutes before kickoff on Saturday. Weather forecast for the game in Norman If you're making the trip to Oklahoma this weekend, be sure to pack an umbrella and a jacket. Temperatures aren't expected to surpass 64 degrees and will dip into the mid-50s. There will be thick cloud cover with a touch of rain, per Accuweather's 10-day forecast. There's a 55% chance of rain all day Saturday for the Norman area. Top storylines Three's a streak: A win over Oklahoma on Saturday would give South Carolina its third straight win. The Gamecocks haven't won three consecutive SEC games since they ended the 2024 season with four straight SEC wins. That six-game winning streak to close out the 2024 season was also the last time the Gamecocks won three games in a row. Should USC beat Oklahoma, it would get the Gamecocks' SEC record back to .500. Sellers needs help in the run game: Make no mistake, South Carolina still has the No. 1 rushing offense in the SEC. The Gamecocks are averaging 218 yards per game, but things haven't looked perfect in recent weeks. Anyone not named LaNorris Sellers has had trouble consistently running the ball for South Carolina. Sellers has accounted for 313 of the 480 rushing yards the Gamecocks have compiled in the last three games. That's certainly good, but USC's running backs need to get going so all the pressure isn't on Sellers' legs down the stretch. Ranking on the horizon? South Carolina received votes in both the Associated Press Top 25 and USA Today Coaches Poll this week after beating Tennessee. USC received 12 votes from the coaches and eight votes from the media. Will a win over Oklahoma be enough to catapult USC into the national rankings for the first time since September 2025? Only time will tell. South Carolina and Oklahoma players to watch South Carolina K Malik Orsan: The sophomore was South Carolina's savior last week. Orsan drilled a 48-yard field goal to help the Gamecocks beat then-No. 11 Tennessee 27-24 as the clock expired. The Southeast Missouri State transfer wasn't necessarily considered to be the top kicker on the roster during USC's kicking competition this offseason. But he's quickly proven why he won the starting job by going 10 for 12 on field goal attempts and 22 for 22 on extra-point attempts this season. South Carolina OL Nolan Hay: The fifth-year offensive lineman was named the Outland Trophy National Player of the Week on Tuesday by the Football Writers Association of America. Hay has been one of the best offensive linemen for the Gamecocks this year. He typically starts at guard but has played some center in Carter Miller's absence because of injury. Hay's Pro Football Focus blocking grade is one of the best on the team. Oklahoma QB John Mateer: There was some buzz around Mateer's name this offseason, but he's found himself in a bit of a rut in 2026. Mateer has thrown for 1,591 yards and 11 touchdowns but has also thrown seven interceptions. He's got a strong arm and is capable of using his legs in the ground game, but has been generally turnover-prone this season. Oklahoma WR Isaiah Sategna III: Sategna was an All-SEC player last year after finishing with 965 receiving yards. The fifth-year student has been Mateer's favorite target in 2026. Sategna leads Oklahoma with 41 catches and 578 yards.

Injuries have once again been a key storyline for the Sooners in the 2026 season. If the key players listed as questionable and probable can be available for this week, it would give the Sooners a boost on both sides of the football. home.blurb: Mississippi State's offense looked out of sorts last week against LSU without Kamario Taylor, as the Bulldogs' offense was shut out for the first time in six seasons. Initial signs from Wednesday's SEC player availability report signaled ... maybe. Taylor remained listed as questionable for the Bulldogs' SEC matchup against the Sooners, according to Friday's player availability report. as he continues to recover from an undisclosed injury. Pete Thamel reported on Oct. 24 , however, Taylor will in fact be playing through his malady against the Sooners. Taylor was listed as questionable on Mississippi State's initial SEC player availability report on Wednesday for Saturday's game vs. Oklahoma. He remained questionable on Friday, but according to Pete Thamel, he will play against Oklahoma. Taylor was downgraded to out ahead of last Saturday's game against LSU due to an undisclosed injury. Before kickoff, he was seen wearing street clothes and a walking boot on the sideline. home.headline: Key Sooners on offense trending toward playing vs. Mississippi State
home.blurb: The Oklahoma Sooners saw some positive movement in the SEC's Thursday evening availability report . Wide receiver Parker Livingstone and running back Tory Blaylock were moved to probable ahead of Saturday's matchup with Mississippi State . Livingstone missed the Kentucky game and will likely need to play a big role for the Sooners with Elijah Thomas still questionable on Thursday night. If Thomas isn't able to go, that puts Manny Choice getting his second straight start on the outside along with Isaiah Sategna in the slot. Livingstone would have a great shot to start on the outside in three-wide receiver sets. All eyes are still on left tackle Michael Fasusi, who remained questionable Thursday night. With Ryan Fodje out, it's critical that Fasusi plays this week against Mississippi State. If he can't go, look for Peyton Joseph to get the start at left tackle. But that would leave a whole at right guard, unless Heath Ozaeta, who is also questionable, can play. Hoping to make his return is cornerback Eli Bowen. Bowen has been out since a practice injury suffered before the Texas game. But Oklahoma could use his speed and coverage ability as the Sooners get set to take on a speedy Bulldogs wide receiver group. Blaylock carried the ball seven times for 23 yards and ran with patience and burst. It was the best he has looked since the College Football Playoff loss to Alabama. Platooning him with Lloyd Avant and Jonathan Hatton helped create a more effective running game than we've had this season. Now the running back room has to build on it. For the Mississippi State Bulldogs , there was no movement on star quarterback Kamario Taylor and running back Fluff Bothwell. Both players missed Mississippi State 31-0 shutout at the hands of the LSU Tigers in Week 7. If they can't play, that significantly increases Oklahoma's chances of earning a win on the road this week. If they do play, the Sooners offense will be under pressure to score to keep pace with Jeff Lebby's offense in Starkville. Here's a look at the Thursday night availability report. Noles247.com staff predictions for Florida State's game against Clemson at Doak Campbell Stadium in Tallahassee, Fla. on Saturday evening: There are many things telling me to pick Florida State in this game. I came away largely unimpressed with Clemson on film – especially the offensive side of the football – the Seminoles are coming off a double-overtime loss to the now top-ranked team in the country (and a bye that followed), and will be at home before heading out for their final two road games of the season against Boston College and Pitt. But there's one thing I keep coming back to. Because of the Tigers' defense, which is still more than solid, I expect this game to be close, and that seems to be a challenge for Mike Norvell's Florida State teams. Since 2024, the Seminoles are 1-9 in games decided by less than one score, which now includes seven straight losses after coming up short again in Miami. Tait Reynolds and company will give Florida State one of the biggest offensive advantages they'll have against a Power Four opponent this season. But Clemson has a defense built to make things difficult for Ashton Daniels , with aggressive pressure packages and sticky man-coverage defenders like Ashton Hampton on the back end. And without running back Ousmane Kromah for the first time, I'm still unsure of how reliably the Seminoles will be able to stay ahead of the sticks without the pure-effort yards that he gave them play after play. Florida State should have every reason and ability to win this football game on Saturday night. Still, when the pressure has increased and Norvell's seat has heated up, the Seminoles have delivered standout performances as they did against Virginia and Miami , and when it's cooled, games like the disastrous trip to Louisville have come back around. This isn't the same Clemson team I grew up watching, but I still believe that Dabo Swinney knows how to win football games, and I'm not so sure that Norvell does. Prediction: Clemson 20, Florida State 17 A clash of titans. A matchup for the ages. Clemson's putrid offense vs. Florida State's complete inability to string together 2 good performances in a row. We've got a very resistible force meeting a completely movable object thing going here. And it's all brought to you by the venerable ACC Network. Pull out your MRE Bucket and get your Alien Tape ready for this one folks! Prediction: Clemson 23, Florida State 20 When I watch Clemson in 2026, it reminds me of FSU in 2024 from an offensive standpoint. A pretty terrible offensive line and issues with the delivery system. It is sort of incredible to see the Tigers struggle so mightily on offense, and especially when looking at them having a capable back in Gideon Davidson and talent among their pass catchers, led by wide receiver Bryant Wesco Jr. Dabo Swinney's bunch is good on defense. Capable of terrorizing the opposing quarterback. Good talent at every level. Cornerback Ashton Hampton is a dude and he leads a nicely revamped secondary. I'm interested in FSU's offense without running back Ousmane Kromah banging out tough yards and extending plays. I think the onus of FSU's rushing attack against Clemson may fall on the shoulders of Ashton Daniels . I expect a fairly low-scoring affair. Clemson will settle for field goals. As long as FSU doesn't gift them a touchdown - via turnover, brutally short field, or massive defensive miscues - I think it will be tough for the Tigers to break 20. If they do, they will win. But I don't think they do it at Doak Campbell on Saturday evening. Prediction: Florida State 24, Clemson 19 Two once proud programs now more laughing stock in the ACC for a variety of reasons. Florida State is receiving praise for trying hard in games. Clemson can't complete a forward pass. Both unranked in October is a real shame and their leaderships should be ashamed of themselves. Florida States offense has a pulse at least and that'll be the difference in this one. It'll be ugly without Ousmane Kromah though. Prediction: Florida State 24, Clemson 13 Kolby Crawford I feel like I've got a decent beat on this team. Typically coming off an open week, I'd be all in on Norvell and the Noles. But this is a must-win spot for Dabo, and Clemson still has what I think is the best player on the field in Ashton Hampton , plus a very competent defensive front. Clemson's offense has been suspect, but I think Tait Reynolds can distribute enough to the playmakers to sneak one out on Halloween night in Doak. Prediction: Clemson 26, Florida State 24 I'm conflicted. Clemson isn't very good. Their offense is probably the most underperforming offense since 2024 FSU. They don't have a consistent presence at QB, and the freshman they're running with is not ready for the pace of the game. He is slow to make decisions and they clearly don't trust him to push the ball down field. Their defense, while good, gets worn down through the course of a game and has some major issues as well. They've let up explosives fairly often in the run game and are one of the worst teams in the country at defending screens. However, I would never doubt a Mike Norvell coached team's ability to lose a game. It's not a stretch to imagine this defense giving up more yards to a mediocre QB. I'm fact, the did it to NMSU's QB earlier this year. Luckily for them, however, this game is at home. The only place they know how to win. They are 8-3 at home and 0-8 away in the past two seasons. That's a pretty safe betting line for me going forward. picks.blurb: Clemson (4-3, 3-2 ACC) is coming off a last-minute 20-16 loss to the Virginia Tech Hokies at Memorial Stadium. The Tigers led for much of the second half, but Hokies quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer led his team on an 11-play, 69-yard drive for the game-winning score with 1:44 to play. Grunkmeyer's 5-yard touchdown pass to tight end Luke Reynolds on fourth-and-1 gave Virginia Tech its first win over Clemson in 19 years and dropped the Tigers to 2-8 in their last 10 home games against Power Four opponents. The offense struggled once again, netting only 288 total yards and going 3 of 14 on third downs. Freshman QB Tait Reynolds completed 20 of his 26 passes, but his average completion went for only 5.9 yards. The Tigers rank dead last in the ACC and just 115th nationally in total offense with 333.1 yards per game. Clemson will face a Florida State (3-4, 1-3) team fresh off a bye, and one that should be playing with plenty of confidence. Mike Norvell's Seminoles took the top-ranked Miami Hurricanes into double overtime before falling 43-35 at Hard Rock Stadium on Oct. 17. Fifth-year senior Ashton Daniels leads the Seminoles' passing attack and has 1,618 yards and 12 touchdowns to eight interceptions in seven games this season. Daniels threw four touchdown passes and rushed for another score in FSU's loss to Miami in Week 7. Clemson has won nine of the last 10 meetings against Florida State dating back to 2015. Will the Tigers' run of dominance in the rivalry continue or end Saturday in Tallahassee? Will Clemson football beat Florida State? ESPN's prediction Oddsmakers have Florida State as a 6.5-point favorite over Clemson, but as always, ESPN Analytics has its own odds for Saturday's game. ESPN's matchup predictor , which offers a prediction model based on its college football power index and other variables, doesn't favor the Tigers, either. It gives Florida State a 71.9% chance to win and Clemson a 28.1% chance. The Tigers are 51st nationally in ESPN's FPI with a 5.8 rating, which ranks 11th among the 17 ACC teams. Florida State has a 10.1 FPI rating that's 37th nationally. The Tigers are one spot ahead of Kansas State (5.7) and one spot below Virginia (6.0). Ratings and projections update daily. FPI data from seasons prior to 2019 may not be complete." picks.blurb: Clemson (4-3, 2-2 ACC) and Florida State (3-4, 1-3), which have played every year since 1992 with the exception of 2020, are both at a crossroads. Neither program wants to move on from its coach and pay a hefty buyout, but neither team has shown very much on the field lately to offer hope. The Tigers suffered a 20-16 gut-punch loss to Virginia Tech in Week 8. It marked Clemson's eighth in its last 10 games against a Power Four opponent at home. The Tigers led for much of the second half until Ethan Grunkemeyer's game-winning 5-yard touchdown pass on fourth-and-1 with 1:44 left. Florida State came within a play or two of adding to the chaos that was college football's thrilling Week 7 slate. The Seminoles took Miami to double overtime before falling 43-35 at Hard Rock Stadium. FSU quarterback Ashton Daniels accounted for five touchdowns in the loss, including four through the air. Clemson hasn't thrown four touchdowns all season. Tait Reynolds, the 19-year-old true freshman who was thrust into the starting job following an injury to Christopher Vizzina, is averaging just 6.1 yards per completion and has been sacked 20 times in seven games behind a weak offensive line. Clemson ranks 115th nationally in total offense with 333.1 yards per game, which is last in the ACC. Florida State ranks 49th with 414.3 total yards per games. Here's ESPN's prediction for Saturday's game. Will Clemson football beat Florida State? ESPN's final score prediction Ahead of Clemson-Florida State, ESPN's Bill Connelly predicted the final score using his popular SP+ metrics . Connelly has the Seminoles winning their first game against the Tigers at Doak Campbell Stadium since 2014. The oddsmakers' latest 5.5 spread favors FSU, as well. Connelly's final score prediction: Florida State 27, Clemson 24. He gives the Seminoles a win probability of 59%. Where Clemson, Florida State sit in ESPN SP+ rankings entering Week 9 rivalry Clemson is No. 55 in ESPN's SP+ team rankings , up one spot from last week despite the loss to Virginia Tech. The Tigers have an overall rating of 4.7, up from 4.0 a week ago. Clemson is one spot ahead of UCF in ESPN's overall team rankings. To break down Clemson's rating by unit, SP+ gives the Tigers a 23.3 rating on offense (No. 97 nationally, up one spot from last week) and a 19.0 rating on defense, which is 25th nationally and is the same as before the Tigers' loss to the Hokies. In special teams, Clemson has a 0.5 rating, which ranks 10th-best in the nation. Florida State is No. 54 in the SP+ team rankings with an overall rating of 5.8, one spot below Virginia and one ahead of Clemson. The metrics give the Seminoles a 32.7 rating on offense that's No. 32 nationally, a 27.1 rating on defense that's No. 76, and a 0.2 rating in special teams that's 43rd in the country. What are ESPN SP+ rankings? According to Connelly, SP+ is "simply a measure of the most sustainable and predictable aspects of football. If you're lucky or unimpressive in a win, your rating will probably fall. If you're strong and unlucky in a loss, it will probably rise." "SP+ is not a résumé ranking, so it does not automatically give credit for big wins or particularly brave scheduling -- no good predictive system does," he adds. picks.blurb: Clemson Predicted to Drop Another Game vs Florida State This Week ClemsonRoundtable 144 Members • 1,122 Posts ClemsonRoundtable ClemsonRoundtable Related stories Trending stories Ken Ruinard / USA Today Network South Ca Ken Ruinard / USA Today Network South Ca Clemson Predicted to Drop Another Game vs Florida State This Week Matt Levine Partner Oct 29, 2026 7:43 PM Published Oct 29, 2026 7:43 PM The Clemson Tigers could be in some trouble this weekend. The Clemson Tigers will be heading out on the road for a big game against the Florida State Seminoles this week. Clemson comes into the contest with a record of 4-3 on the season, having lost last week to Virginia Tech. Florida State will be entering the game with a record of 3-4 for the season, looking to defend home field this week. In a new prediction from college football analyst David Kenyon of Bleacher Report , Clemson will struggle in this game against Florida State. Kenyon has the Tigers dropping the game to the Seminoles by a score of 24-19. If this prediction were to come true, it would send the Tigers into some real trouble, with them falling to 4-4 on the season. There have already been calls for head coach Dabo Swinney to be let go of before the year started, and if the team can't turn things around, it will only grow louder. Related stories For Clemson to avoid dropping the game to Florida State, the offense is going to have to get going. The Tigers have been carried by their defense all season long, with the offensive attack falling way behind. Quarterback Tait Reynolds has struggled in his first action in college, and he has limited what this Tigers team can do. For the year, Reynolds has thrown for just 1,096 yards with one touchdown and three interceptions. Reynolds has seen problems trying to push the ball down the field, and the offense has been ineffective due to this. Clemson has to find some sort of footing offensively if they want to take down Florida State on the road this week. Due to the struggles of Reynolds, there have been calls for the Tigers to make a switch at the quarterback position. But for now, Swinney seems content to go with Reynolds, even though he had previously said that a change could be made. Christopher Vizzina entered the year as the starter, but was then benched after just two weeks for Reynolds. Vizzina did suffer an injury, but he has remained on the bench due to performance, according to Swinney. If the Tigers were to drop this game to the Seminoles, the calls for Vizzina to return would likely continue. Swinney would then have some choices to make, especially with the season starting to spiral out of control for the team. Kickoff for the game between the Tigers and Seminoles is scheduled for 4:00 p.m. PT/7:00 p.m. ET from Doak S. Campbell Stadium.

away.headline: DT Vic Burley added to injury report for Clemson vs Virginia Tech
away.blurb: Burley, a senior, was listed as questionable again after being added Oct. 22. He was not listed on the initial report Oct. 21. Burley has played in four games after missing the first two because of a suspension. He got his first tackle, a sack, in Week 7 vs Georgia Southern. Clemson wide receiver Gordon Sellars III is listed as out. Tigers coach Dabo Swinney said that Sellars has a concussion and is going through concussion protocol. He's made three catches for 8 yards in a backup role. Defensive tackle Devarrick Woods and running back Jarvis Green don't appear on the injury report for Clemson. Swinney has said that he expects both players to return from injury against Virginia Tech. Vizzina was removed from the Tigers' injury report against California on Sept. 25 ahead of kickoff that night and hasn't appeared once since. However, Vizzina hasn't fully recovered, and he was only available for emergencies against Miami and Charleston Southern. Clemson football defensive tackle Vic Burley remained on the injury report Oct. 23 for the Tigers' game vs Virginia Tech. The Tigers (4-2, 2-1 ACC) square off with Virginia Tech (5-2, 2-2) at home on Oct. 24 (7 p.m., ESPN). Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. Christopher Vizzina injury update Swinney said backup quarterback Christopher Vizzina is having his "best week by far" of the season and that he's 90% healthy. Vizzina has been recovering from a small fracture in his left elbow after originally injuring it against Georgia Southern on Sept. 12. Swinney said after the Charleston Southern game that he wouldn't have had an issue with playing Vizzina against the Buccaneers, but that Vizzina told him he wasn't ready and that Brock Bradley should enter instead. Trent Pearman and Bradley entered, respectively, after Clemson pulled starter Tait Reynolds with the game well in hand. "I asked him. I said, 'Do you want to go in, or do you want to put Brock in?' And he's like, 'Let's put Brock in,'" Swinney said. "So that was really his call. Coach C.V." home.headline: Florida State injury updates: Mike Norvell expects key returns, but timing is an issue
home.blurb: Florida State coach Mike Norvell recently provided a couple of injury updates on multiple Seminoles who have missed significant time this season. Injuries have been a huge issue for the team this year for Norvell, particularly on defense, where multiple players are out for the season. Sometimes injuries can make or break a team, and so far, the Seminoles have been able to do quite a bit with multiple contributors sidelined. Norvell kicked off his injury updates portion of the press conference with a quick tidbit on linebacker Blake Nichelson, who has not played since the season opener against New Mexico State. Nichelson is nearing a return, and while the game against Clemson might still be out of reach , the linebacker should be able to return to play soon. Samuel Singleton Jr.'s return would be huge for the Florida State offense Norvell is not giving up on Singleton's return; he never ruled the running back out for the season, and he clearly still thinks there is hope for his return. It might be a delusion at this point from Norvell to avoid the reality that Florida State is in a bad spot at running back, or a future return this season might still truly be in the cards. I personally would like to think that Singleton is close to coming back, and the faster he can return, the better for Florida State. Tre Wisner is an experienced running back, but he has not been the most effective player in a short sample size this season. Aside from Wisner, there is not much of an experienced supporting cast. Additionally, Florida State might be in trouble if Singleton is not able to return this season due to the fact that there are only three healthy running backs. The Seminoles truly cannot afford to have another running back go down with an injury, and if Singleton is not available for another two or three weeks, that could be an issue. The timing of Crutchfield's return could not be any better, with Quindarrius Jones, Nehemiah Chandler, and Ashlynd Barker all dealing with injuries. Barker has been playing through his injury thanks to a cast, but Crutchfield can do it all in the secondary, and he should be able to take some pressure off multiple players. home.headline: Quindarrius Jones injury update: Florida State's banged-up secondary continues to take hits
home.blurb: With the game against Clemson quickly approaching for Florida State, a top defensive back has been ruled out. Starting corner Quindarrius Jones left the game against Miami in Week 7 after playing just 14 snaps. Jones had a week to recover with the bye, which brought some hope, but the defender will not be able to play against Clemson. Jones has missed two games this season now after sitting out the home game against Central Arkansas earlier in the year. Frankly, it was better for the defense to play Central Arkansas without him, so more defensive backs would be able to see the field. However, against Clemson, Florida State cannot afford to suffer another injury at an already weak position. The secondary has been torn to shreds all year, with Karson Hobbs and Jamari Howard spending the majority of the season on the injury report. Jones has missed time, freshman Jordan Crutchfield has been unavailable most of the season, and Chuck Kennon was dismissed just as he began to recover from an injury. With Jones out, two players will likely take over: Charles Lester III and Jordan Crutchfield, who will be making his return from an injury against Clemson. Lester has been the main replacement for Jones this season, playing 33 snaps against Miami after Jones left the game. Lester also replaced Jones for the game against Central Arkansas, logging 34 snaps. Jones typically plays between 45 and 55 snaps each week, with his total number of snaps played increasing as the injuries in the secondary have stacked up. Lester has been covering a good portion of the missing snaps, but against Miami, Ja'Bril Rawls played 74 out of 80 possible snaps, which is something he has done multiple times this season. Lester is more than likely going to resume the same role he has previously taken when Jones is forced to sit out, but the addition of a healthy Crutchfield gives the staff options. Fellow safety KJ Kirkland is expected to play, but has been dealing with an injury, which could create a different avenue to the field for Crutchfield. In limited playing time this season, Lester has proven to be effective at times, with eight total tackles, including three against Miami after Jones left the game. Lester has struggled at times in coverage, but his ability to recover and limit additional gains is notable. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings Miami looks to stay unbeaten against a sneaky-good North Carolina team on the road Getty Images Prior to last week, Miami had not held the No. 1 spot in the AP Top 25 poll since 2002, but so far the Hurricanes are looking every bit the part of the best team in the country. Not only have they raced out to a 7-0 start this year, but they've done so in a way that suggests a continuation of the success that led Miami all the way to the national championship game last season. With a 14-1 record in its last 15 games, Miami has been one of the best teams in the country since early November 2025, and now each week provides yet another opportunity for this year's team to validate that high poll ranking. This week, that means a trip to Chapel Hill to take on Bill Belichick and North Carolina in a game that offers Cristobal and Miami a chance to reverse a recent skid in the series. The Tar Heels have won their last five meetings in the series, including a 2-0 record against Cristobal with wins in 2022 and 2023. But those two Miami teams finished a combined 12-13 overall, while this year's group is clearly playing on a different level. For starters, those teams didn't have not just one but two Heisman Trophy contenders like Miami does this year with quarterback Darian Mensah and wide receiver Malachi Toney . Those last teams that lost to North Carolina also didn't carry the nation's best scoring margin, as Miami does currently, beating opponents by 33.7 points per game. There's some history that favors UNC, sure, but Miami's strength will challenge the impact of the past. Miami vs. North Carolina: Need to know Tar Heels looking to bounce back from upset home loss: While Miami validated its position at No. 1 last week with a thorough thrashing of Pitt, North Carolina saw some of the hype for this matchup cooled by an upset loss at home to Syracuse . The Tar Heels led by 10 points in the fourth quarter but let Steve Angeli and the Orange offense back into the game with a couple late scores before eventually falling in overtime. That's brought even more urgency to Bill Belichick's crew to have their game locked in for Saturday night, because the kind of failure at the margins that led to the fourth-quarter collapse will only be exposed more dramatically against a team of Miami's caliber. The Tar Heels have shown in wins over TCU , Pitt and Duke that they can play a tight game and come out on the right side of close margins, but those victories (and certainly any upset effort against Miami) require a cleaner effort than North Carolina showed against Syracuse last week. A Saturday showcase spot for Miami's Heisman Trophy contenders: Miami has a nice two-week run where its opponents and the stage will allow for quarterback Darian Mensah and wide receiver Malachi Toney to receive a big-time spotlight in the national conversation. This week's game against North Carolina, on Halloween night in Chapel Hill, will draw plenty of attention and could allow the Hurricanes (who are 14-point favorites) to continue building the resumes of both Mensah and Toney. Mensah is putting together one of the best starts to a season we have seen from a quarterback this century, currently leading the nation in completion percentage (81.4%) while also rolling up 22 passing touchdowns (2nd in FBS) and 307.3 passing yards per game (fourth in FBS). Malachi Toney, meanwhile, leads the FBS in receptions (66) and has become the first wide receiver with at least 900 receiving yards and 10 receiving touchdowns on a 7-0 team since eventual Heisman winner DeVonta Smith in 2020. Miami is elite in the middle (of games): It's easy to look at the collection of talent Mario Cristobal has assembled as an explanation for the team's dominance, but that talent has to perform to deliver the kind of results the Hurricanes have been getting over the last two seasons. Part of winning big has been winning small, and for Miami that's included dominating the middle portions of games. The Hurricanes have the No. 1 point differential in the second quarter in all of FBS (+95) and No. 3 point differential in the third quarter (+57). Miami is also No. 3 nationally this season in "middle 8" scoring (the last four minutes of the second quarter and the first four minutes of the third quarter), with a +7.6-point average on the season. The Hurricanes, ranked No. 4 at the time, were 6-0 and looking to establish themselves as the class of the ACC, having joined the conference just a few years removed from a national championship. A lot has been made about Miami's struggles in the last five meetings, but the Hurricanes' issues with the Heels date back to the very beginning of their time in the league, and Connor Barth's game-winning kick to seal the spooky upset. Bill Belichick and North Carolina's defense can get enough stops to keep this close, and with Notre Dame on deck, the Hurricanes might not be in the mindset to push this game deep into the evening. We're projecting North Carolina to flirt with the cover, but ultimately for the total to come in under the oddsmaker's number. That sets up a game with long drives, fewer possessions, and limited scoring. Miami vs North Carolina combo This combo is essentially asking Miami to control the game early, then let it get ugly. The Hurricanes can come out sharp enough to cover during the first quarter before the pace slows and Belichick starts making adjustments. That still leaves room for North Carolina to hang around inside two touchdowns while the game stays comfortably below the total. That's the sweet spot here. Seven games into the season, Miami has treated its freshmen like battle-tested veterans. The team has put 27 first-year players on the field for offense and defense. These young athletes have logged 2,118 snaps this season. That number ranks second in the Power 4, trailing only USC. Coach Mario Cristobal knows the value of this early time on the field. He refuses to let young players use their age as an excuse for mistakes. "The value of getting guys experience is really valuable," Cristobal said, according to Sun Sentinel . He made it clear that the team expects these kids to perform now. The mindset of waiting for them to learn later is simply not an option for Miami. Running back Javian Mallory has turned into a star for the Hurricanes. The freshman from West Boca Raton High leads the team with 444 rushing yards. He has scored seven rushing touchdowns, which ties him with veteran Mark Fletcher Jr. Mallory is averaging 7.5 yards every time he carries the ball. Pro Football Focus gives him an 87 rushing grade. This marks him as the fourth-best true freshman in the country. While Mallory shines, the offensive line faces some tough tests. Starting left guard Ben Congdon has had a mixed start to his career. He is a large player at 6-foot-8 and 330 pounds. Pro Football Focus gives him a 55 grade for run blocking but only a 32.2 grade for pass protection. Last week against Pittsburgh, he allowed four pressures and one sack. Cristobal defended his young lineman despite the struggles against a tough Pitt front. "He's played good football. I think this past week was … not his overall best performance, but he did do some good things," Cristobal said. The coach noted that reacting to fast defensive stunts is hard for anyone. He believes Congdon and the other linemen are a key reason for the team's offensive success. Quarterback Accuracy Under Pressure Quarterback Darian Mensah brings a different kind of value to the roster. His ability to throw accurately while under pressure is his main strength. Mensah leads all quarterbacks with an 81.4 completion percentage this year. He is even better when teams send extra pass rushers his way. According to reports, he completes 89.7 percent of his passes when facing blitzes. This leads the nation among quarterbacks blitzed 30 or more times. home.headline: North Carolina Dealing With Unknown Injury to Matt Able
home.blurb: I'd be worried if he doesn't play a lot in the first month or so, though. UNC has a need to get better as a team with all the new faces and a different system. The last thing the program needs is for one of the best players on the roster to be out. North Carolina Dealing With Unknown Injury to Matt Able TarHeelsRoundtable 160 Members • 1,563 Posts TarHeelsRoundtable TarHeelsRoundtable Related stories IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect North Carolina Dealing With Unknown Injury to Matt Able Jon Conahan Partner Oct 29, 2026 4:00 PM Published Oct 29, 2026 4:00 PM Able has to get healthy for UNC. North Carolina fans are ready for the college basketball season, but a couple of things need to be considered before Monday night as it takes on Western Carolina. North Carolina should be able to win this game no matter who's on the court for them, but it's also important to note that some injuries are currently being factored in. The biggest is Matt Able, the North Carolina State transfer expected to be one of the better players on the roster this season. Able missed the exhibition game against Charlotte, though it hasn't been reported yet what happened. According to Rodd Baxley, who was at the game, the injury didn't look noticeable. Baxley added that he was on the sidelines during UNC's warmups, and it didn't seem to be too big of a problem. “Able, an N.C. State transfer, is one of 11 newcomers on coach Michael Malone's first roster in Chapel Hill. The 6-foot-5, 200-pound guard is a starter in the backcourt alongside Virginia Tech transfer Neo Avdalas and Utah transfer Terrence Brown… “Able's injury doesn't look noticeable. He was on the sidelines during UNC's warmups ahead of the game. Still, it's another missed opportunity for Able to get game action with a revamped roster and a backcourt that includes Utah transfer Terrence Brown, along with Virginia Tech transfer Neo Avdalas. Isaiah Denis missed the Indiana exhibition game with a minor injury,” Baxley wrote . Able, who withdrew from the NBA draft last year to go to North Carolina, is expected to be one of the ACC's better players this season. He's coming off a decent freshman year at NC State, averaging 8.8 points, 3.4 rebounds, and shooting 35.5% from three-point range on 4.1 attempts per game. He has areas to improve, including as a passer, but there's a lot to like about the young man, and the hope is that he'll be what everybody knows he can be. Hopefully, this is just a small thing, and North Carolina can get it under control before it plays on Monday night. If not, it's fine if he misses a few games.

home.headline: Miami returns to all-white stormtroopers for Halloween Night trip to North Carolina
home.blurb: Miami returns to all-white stormtroopers for Halloween night trip to North Carolina Skip to main content About Hurricanes All-Time Football Lists Hurricanes All-Time Basketball Lists Miami Hurricanes Basketball Recruiting The Joe Gaither Show on CanesCentral The Miami Hurricanes will wear their all-white "Stormtrooper" combination for Saturday night's Halloween game against the North Carolina Tar Heels. Miami announced the look on Thursday, pairing white helmets with white jerseys and white pants (the program's standard road uniform). The No. 1 Hurricanes are undefeated in the combination this season after road wins at Stanford (45-6), Wake Forest (33-20) and Clemson (41-13). All white, all business 🙌 pic.twitter.com/dpVbfdILLx North Carolina enters at 4-3 overall and 2-2 in ACC play, while Miami (7-0, 5-0 ACC) arrives as a two-touchdown favorite. The Hurricanes are seeking their first win in Chapel Hill since 2017 and first victory in the series since 2018. North Carolina has won the past five meetings and holds a series edge 16-11. The Hurricanes have largely stuck to a simple rotation. The all-white Stormtroopers have served as the primary road look, and at home they have worn the traditional white helmet, orange jersey and white pants combination against Florida A&M and Florida State. The green alternate (white helmet, green jersey, green pants) appeared once, in a 52-3 win over Central Michigan. Last week against Pittsburgh, Miami debuted the home version of its 2001 Tribute throwbacks to honor the 25th anniversary of the 2001 national championship team. The road version of those throwbacks (white jersey with green pants) has not yet been used. They have met 24 times in their history, though a lot of those meetings have come in bowl games. In fact, they have played nearly as many games against one another in Pasadena at the Rose Bowl (7) as they have in Los Angeles at the Coliseum (8). What they have not done, however, is face each other as conference mates. Their last meeting came in the 2017 Cotton Bowl. Prior to that, they hadn't played since the 2009 season. It took until USC's third season as a Big Ten member for the two to appear on each other's schedules, but this Saturday night the wait will end. And it's a game that got a lot more intriguing in recent weeks. USC enters the game unranked for the first time all season following a 17-7 loss at Wisconsin last week. While Ohio State remains second in the AP Top 25, this will be the team's first game since losing starting quarterback Julian Sayin , who was knocked out of their 19-15 win over Indiana . Ohio State vs. USC: Need to know This will be Luke Fahey's first career start: On the surface, giving your quarterback his first career start on the road is not an ideal situation, but it's one Ohio State has had success with before. In 2001, Craig Krenzel started his first game on the road against Michigan of all teams, and Ohio State won that game 26-20. In 2013, it was Kenny Guiton winning his first start at Cal, and in 2021, CJ Stroud won his first start at Minnesota . There's a lot on the line for Jeremiah Smith : Smith is the best receiver in the country and is already Ohio State's all-time leader in career receptions, yards, and touchdowns, just to name a few stats. He's also the clear favorite to win the Heisman Trophy, but this will be his first start with Fahey as well. It's safe to assume Smith will be Fahey's preferred target, but it remains to be seen whether he can maintain the same level of production and how that may impact his Heisman chances. USC is 9-2 at home in Big Ten games since joining the league: I started with the good part. The bad news is that the Trojans are only 1-2 at home in Big Ten games against ranked opponents. They're 5-14 overall against ranked teams under Lincoln Riley, and Jayden Maiava is 1-5 as a starter against them. The lone win came last season at home against Michigan. The smarter play is to attack the total. It's safe to assume Ohio State's offense will struggle a bit, and they'll probably lean on the run game a lot more to take pressure off Fahey. We've also seen USC's offense struggle in games against ranked opponents. away.headline: Where Ohio State football’s offensive line health stands going into USC game
away.blurb: However, Daniels was injured late in a Sept. 12 loss at Texas. He did not return until an Oct. 17 win at Indiana. COLUMBUS, Ohio — Ohio State football fielded a variety of offensive line combinations through the first half of its regular season, with injuries forcing movement up front. Coming off a bye week and heading into Saturday’s game at USC, coach Ryan Day expects the unit to be as healthy as it has been this season. “We should have a full week of practice and a full arsenal of guys up front, so that is a huge deal going into this game,” Day said during a radio hit Monday on 97.1 The Fan. “We know that the offensive line, we’re going to lean on them more to be the guys who lead this team — along with our seniors, along with Jeremiah (Smith), running backs that are running real hard. But it all starts up front.” The Buckeyes opened the season with Ian Moore, Luke Montgomery, Carson Hinzman, Austin Siereveld and Phillip Daniels starting from left to right. During his absence, Ohio State originally moved Siereveld to right tackle and started Gabe VanSickle at right guard. That changed Oct. 10, when an illness sidelined Siereveld hours before a matchup with Maryland. VanSickle moved to right tackle and Jake Cook started at right guard as a result. The Buckeyes moved VanSickle back to right guard when Daniels returned to play right tackle the following week. The starting combination with a full roster remains unclear, though Day said Siereveld would start at tackle if healthy when asked ahead of the Indiana game. Health up front is always paramount, but that is especially true for a team making a change at quarterback. Julian Sayin was injured late in the win at Indiana, and the Buckeyes are preparing for him to miss the remainder of the season. As a result, freshman Luke Fahey or sophomore Tavien St. Clair will start Saturday at USC. “These guys have played a lot of football before,” Day said of the offensive line. “We’re in that huddle and you’ve got a young quarterback right there — I mean, they’re going to be looking to him, but he’s going to be looking at them. I’ve got to give them credit already. They’re already building up the confidence of our young quarterbacks.” ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. away.headline: DB Jay Timmons among Ohio State starters questionable for USC game
away.blurb: News Sports Business Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL DB Jay Timmons among Ohio State starters questionable for USC game Brianna Mac Kay Columbus Dispatch Oct. 28, 2026, 8:56 p.m. ET Along with quarterback Julian Sayin and running back Ja'Kobi Jackson , Ohio State football could be without two more starters for the USC game on Oct. 31. Ohio State nickel back Jay Timmons and wide receiver Brandon Inniss are listed as questionable on the Buckeyes ' initial availability report, released by the Big Ten three days before the game. Sayin and Jackson are the only starters among seven Buckeyes already ruled out. Freshman wide receiver Brock Boyd is also listed as questionable. Sayin and Jackson were expected to be out for the USC game, as Sayin is out "indefinitely" with an undisclosed injury he suffered in the fourth quarter of the Indiana game and Jackson underwent foot surgery, according to a report from ESPN on Oct. 21. Timmons made his first appearance in two games against Indiana on Oct. 17 , recording seven tackles, two pass breakups and a forced fumble. But Timmons was pulled from the lineup once again and missed Ohio State's final defensive drives due to an apparent injury. "He plans on traveling," Ohio State coach Ryan Day said Oct. 28. "We'll kind of see how the next couple of days go." After Inniss had missed the Maryland matchup on Oct. 10 with an undisclosed injury, he played the full game against Indiana , logging one catch for 6 yards. The senior is tied for third for the Buckeyes with 11 receptions this season for 158 yards and one touchdown. Ohio State offensive lineman Austin Siereveld was notably left off the availability report after missing the previous two games due to illness. Day stated that Siereveld has returned to full practice this week, and he expects the senior to be an option, though is uncertain he'll be able to play the full game. The Buckeyes kick off at USC at 7:30 p.m. ET. If you purchase through our links, the USA Today Network may earn a commission. Prices were accurate at the time of publication but may change.

However, Fahey has served as the backup to Sayin all year after he beat out sophomore Tavien St. Clair in the quarterback battle, and he has held that job ever since. Both quarterbacks took reps with the starters over the bye week. Buckeyes fans will have to wait until Saturday to find out who gets the nod, but it would be a surprise if it wasn't Fahey. The Buckeyes' offense runs through Smith first. From there, the running game supplements it with Bo Jackson and now Isaiah West carrying the load with Ja'Kobi Jackson out. picks.headline: Baylor Football Staff Picks: Over/Under Predictions For Week 9 vs. UCF
picks.blurb: Baylor Football Staff Picks: Over/Under Predictions For Week 9 vs. UCF Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL Bears In The Pros Week 9 is here and Baylor could look like a different team when it takes the field. The Bears are headed down to Orlando for a Friday night contest against the Knights . UCF is coming off an incredible overtime win over BYU, which gave the Cougars their first loss of the season. As for Baylor, the Bears fired Dave Aranda in his seventh season at the helm. Joe Klanderman has taken over as interim head coach and Baylor's coaching search is underway . Baylor on SI came up with some game props and picked what might happen on Friday night. DJ Lagway throws for O/U 239.5 passing yards IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Trent Knoop - OVER Trent Knoop - OVER DJ Lagway has been over this total in two of his last four games, but it does appear that Lagway is getting healthier, which only bodes well for the Bears' offense. UCF doesn't have a great passing defense, and with Baylor struggling to run the ball, Lagway will have to throw to win. Bennett Parker - OVER Personally, I would not touch Lagway O/U lines with a six-foot pole. Through seven games, I still don’t know what to think about his arm talent and decision making. It could very well be another 50% completion, ugly game for Lagway. However, if Baylor plays ‘free’ and ‘energized’ like they have been stressing, Lagway will be at his best and cruise past this line with the help of some trusty receivers and their yards after catch ability. Brad Teague - OVER There is absolutely no reason that DJ Lagway should be under 239 passing yards this week. Yes, Dave Aranda was just fired; but OC Jake Spavital has been calling the offensive plays this season, and is allegedly being now given "the freedom to be as creative as he wants to be" as interim head coach Joe Klanderman said during Media Availability on Monday. He only had 236 yards passing against Kansas last week, but I expect Lagway to excel this week against UCF, playing more freely, and finding numerous receivers on his way to having more than 240 yards passing. I'm taking the OVER on this one. Grant Peterson - OVER I’m leaning toward the over on this one. Even in games where Baylor has struggled offensively, Lagway has found a way to cover this line. I also think Jake Spavital will get creative and find ways to open up the passing game for this offense. Tyler Gillum - OVER UCF’s pass defense has been inconsistent this year averaging just about 240 passing yards per game this year. and Lagway hasn't been under 225 since the Colorado game, coming back from injury. Baylor's defense has O/U 2.5 sacks against UCF IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Trent Knoop - UNDER Trent Knoop - UNDER UCF is a top-five team in the Big 12 in sacks allowed. Baylor has an aggressive defense and should get to Keyone Jenkins. But Jenkins is a mobile quarterback who can escape pressure. Scott Frost will dial up some quick passes on Friday in hopes of not allowing Jenkins to stand in the pocket and take heat. The defensive line and linebacker play have been the cornerstone of the Bears’ defense and will continue to be against UCF. Klanderman has sent some well-timed blitzes, and knows how to keep the opposing QB off balance. The Bears had five sacks against Kansas and should at least scare that mark again on Friday. The Bears have the 2nd most sacks in all of the FBS in the first half of games with 17. Baylor has had 3 or more QB sacks in every game except against LA Tech back in September, I don't expect that trend to slow down any time soon. UCF QB Keyone Jenkins, as a playmaker, is going to look to take advantage of Baylor's aggression on the defensive line, but I fully expect Coach Klanderman and the Bears defense to be prepared for exactly that. This game has the potential for a high-count of TFLs, Sks, and FFs . I'm taking an emphatic OVER on this one. Grant Peterson - UNDER Baylor’s defense has been great at generating pressure all season, but I think they’ll finish with two sacks in this matchup. UCF has only allowed more than two sacks in one game this season. The Knights gave up two sacks to both TCU and Houston, along with one sack to BYU and Oklahoma State. Although I’m taking the under, I wouldn’t be surprised to see the Bears come away with three sacks. Tyler Gillum - UNDER Although I do think they can get some pressure on UCF. I think it'll be just about two or maybe even one. Keyone Jenkins showed the ability to escape the pocket and make plays. BYU was able to get just one sack all game with their defense. My prediction is Baylor will likely be the same UCF QB Keyone Jenkins has O/U 250.5 passing yards vs. Baylor Baylor has a good defense, but the Bears have allowed the opposing quarterback to throw for over 251 yards in three of their last four games. Keyone Jenkins has thrown for over 251 yards in his last three outings. The Knights are riding the hot hand and Jenkins' up-tempo style of play can cause some havoc. The Baylor defense has a way of giving up a decent amount of yards without surrendering too many points, allowing 340 per game while averaging just 16.1 points against. The secondary tends to allow some long drives early in the game and the occasional explosive play downfield. I expect UCF to take advantage as much as they can early on. Brad Teague - UNDER He's had some bigger games recently against the 'Pokes (265 yards) and BYU (293 yards), but on the season Keyone Jenkins is only averaging 157 passing yards a game. Not to mention that late in the BYU game, Jenkins would make a visit to the medical tent after being shaken up on a play. There's a chance that his overall drop-backs and longer-developing throws may be limited this week against a Bears defense who will be looking to continue their aggressive gameplay. Provided that Baylor's secondary can limit the penalties being called on them, they're among the top units in all of college football and always hungry for another INT. Keyone Jenkins does not throw for 250 yards in this game; I'm taking the UNDER on this one, Baylor has done a good job of limiting explosive passing plays this season, and I think that trend will continue against UCF. If the Bears can prevent Jenkins from connecting on big plays, I don’t see him surpassing 250 passing yards against this defense. If this game turns into a shootout, he could go over, but I don’t expect that to happen. Although I believe Jenkins will have another solid game, 250 is a lot against this relentless defense. I'm gonna say it'll be just under, but not by much, Jenkins hasn't been under 250 since September against TCU, but the Bears should bring enough pressure for Jenkins to just miss that mark Baylor rushes for O/U 160.5 yards against UCF Until Baylor proves it can run the ball, it's hard to put trust in the run game. It's not due to the running backs themselves. I do think Baylor has a good stable of backs, but the offensive line has been too inconsistent for my liking. This game will come down to DJ Lagway's arm. If Baylor intends on winning this game, they have no choice but to run the ball and run it well. Lagway has shown that he is back to 100% and the O-line is playing with a fire lit under them after struggling in the last couple of games. While I am not convinced by the Bears’ ground game whatsoever, they will get over this total with a lot of help from Lagway. There is zero reason why the Bears shouldn't be able to be well over this mark; except there are, in fact, five reasons why Baylor could miss this target. The Bears offensive line has not had great success this season at fully establishing a solid push and a dominant running game. They're working hard, like to block with and for each other and the Bears team, and seem to be giving it their all; but they've been ineffective throughout most of the season. They've had a 94.5% success rate of keeping the pocket clean on pass plays this season, but have only been able to gain 3.79 rushing yards a carry this season. Currently the Bears are averaging 146.14 rushing yards per game, and unless Dave Aranda getting fired is the catalyst these guys needed to become a stronger unit, I don't see Baylor gaining more than 160 rushing yards; I'm taking the UNDER. Baylor’s running game has been an issue all season, and I don’t expect that to change against the Knights. Against TCU, Baylor averaged just 1.6 yards per carry. Even against Kansas, one of the worst rushing defenses in the conference, the Bears averaged only 3.5 yards per carry, including Lagway’s rushing yards. Based on Baylor’s struggles on the ground this season, I’m taking the under on 160.5 rushing yards. After a rough two weeks of running the ball for Baylor, I don't expect much to change in this one. UCF is coming off a huge win and is ranked 38th in the country in rushing yards allowed on defense. It's going to be a real struggle if the Bears want to move the ball on the ground, and early passing will likely be needed to get any type of momentum on offense. picks.headline: Know Thy Foe: Baylor Expert Shares What UCF Fans Need To Know For Space Game
picks.blurb: Know Thy Foe: Baylor Expert Shares What UCF Fans Need To Know For Space Game Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL RECRUITING COLLEGE FOOTBALL NEWS Olympic Sports More from UCF Knights On SI FOOTBALL While the UCF Knights may be coming off of one of the most significant wins in its program's history against No. 2 BYU on Saturday, they do not have long before they have to follow it up. The Baylor Bears may be entering their first game of the post-Dave Aranda era after firing him on Sunday, but they still have the same record as the Knights, and their interim coach, Joe Klanderman, has been in charge of a defense that has been one of the top five in the nation in sacks and tackles for loss. Jacob Haddaadin is both a Baylor graduate and a contributor for Baylor Bears on SI, and he took some time this week to answer some of our questions about the Bears (4-3, 2-2 Big 12): 1. How did the Bears reach a position in which they ended up firing their head coach midseason? Haddadin: Dave Aranda’s firing wasn't strictly due to this season's results. Ever since Dave Aranda won the Big 12 championship in 2021, the program has slowly trended downward. The Bears had real momentum after beating ASU in Tempe, but that momentum stalled after a double-digit home loss to TCU and a loss to a bad Kansas team in Lawrence. Dave Aranda had a losing record in the Big 12, a 1-6 record against rival TCU, and his teams were consistently unprepared in big games. We are forever grateful for the 12-2 season in 2021, but enough was enough, and Baylor fans were fed up with the constant expectation and disappointment cycle that was Dave Aranda. The loss to Kansas solidified that the Dave Aranda-led team was once again not going to be anything special. Cementing his exit from the program. 2. What’s the rundown on interim coach Joe Klanderman? What made him the choice to lead the program for the remainder of the season? Haddadin: Before Manhattan, Klanderman cut his teeth at North Dakota State, where he spent five years as defensive backs coach from 2014 to 2018, contributing to four FCS national championships. He then spent seven years at Kansas State, six of them running the defense, and K-State maintained a top-30 national ranking in defensive efficiency for five straight seasons through 2025. Part of what made him the choice is continuity. He was brought to Waco as one of the big offseason moves meant to turn things around; he’s already in the building, and the defense he built has been the most reliable part of this team. He has also come in with a clear plan, laying out three priorities for his time as interim head coach: energizing the program, strengthening the roster for 2027, and establishing complementary football to help Baylor win more games. He has been honest about where the problems are, too, pointing to the offensive line and the running game as the areas that need the most work. Whether or not this turns into a permanent job, the next five games give him a real chance to make his case, starting with a Friday night road game at UCF. 3. Quarterback DJ Lagway seems to have really connected with wide receiver Gavin Freeman, the latter of which is second in the nation in receptions per game and 14th in the nation in receiving yards. What makes Freeman such an oft-target wideout? Also, is there anyone else in the Bears’ receiving corps that could step up as a main target if Freeman is well-covered? Haddadin: Gavin Freeman’s production makes sense once you look at what he brings. At 5-9 and 189 pounds, he isn’t going to win many jump balls, but he has been reliable all season. He arrived as a redshirt senior after playing 2022-23 at Oklahoma and 2024-25 at Oklahoma State, and he was already a go-to receiver before coming to Waco, leading the Cowboys with 53 receptions for 481 yards and four scores in 2025. His fit with Lagway was clear from the first game, when he caught 12 passes for 154 yards and a touchdown in his Baylor debut against Auburn. It also helps that during the offseason, observers expected the passing game to work the middle of the field more, since Lagway is more comfortable there than Sawyer Robertson was. That is exactly where a quick, shifty slot receiver like Freeman does his best work. He has also produced when the offense hasn’t: in the 17-6 loss to TCU, he still caught seven passes for 76 yards. He adds value in other ways too. Last year at Oklahoma State, he contributed in both the passing and running game and as a returner. If defenses focus on Freeman, the most likely next option is Louis Brown IV. Before the season, he was described as the leader of the receiver room as one of its few upperclassmen with real experience in the offense, and he and Lagway connected well in the spring. Jadon Porter is another option to watch, and Baylor’s tight ends have been factors in the red zone. 4. Baylor is one of the most penalized teams in the Big 12. Is there one side of the ball that draws more flags? If so, why? Also, is there a particular penalty that gets called a lot? Haddadin: Most of the flags come from the offense, and specifically the offensive line. Through the early home stretch, one count found that the offense was outpacing the defense by nearly 3 to 1 in total penalties. The penalty that keeps showing up is the false start. Baylor had 5 against Prairie View A&M, 3 against Louisiana Tech, and 3 against Colorado, for at least 11 false starts in three home games. The Prairie View game was the low point: all four of Baylor’s false-start penalties were attributed to offensive lineman Asher Hale, and Aranda admitted afterward that one player had a bunch of penalties. Holding calls have added to the problem, but false starts are harder to excuse. ​A big reason is inexperience. The line was overhauled in the offseason and has been banged up in 2026, and while Baylor has capable players at each spot, most are new and started their first games together this year. Injuries haven’t helped either, including the injury to Koltin Sieracki, who was projected to be the best of the bunch but has not produced on the level the staff or fans expected. 5. The Bears have had a knack for getting behind the line of scrimmage this season, ranking in the top five in the nation in both sacks and tackles for loss. Who do they have to thank for that and what helps them get past offensive lines so often this season? Haddadin: The turnaround is remarkable given where this defense was a year ago. Baylor finished last season tied for last in the Big 12 and at the bottom of the FBS in sacks. Much of the credit goes to Klanderman and an offseason rebuild that put NIL money into the roster from the inside out. Defensive end Garrick Ponder leads the team with 3.5 sacks, Ryan Davis has added 2.5 off the edge, and Jordan Mack has chipped in 2.0. Up the middle, Hosea Wheeler and Traevon Mitchell occupy blockers and collapse the pocket, which opens lanes for everyone else. The most telling detail may be that two of the top three sack producers are safeties: Bo Onu and Daniel Cobbs have 3.0 sacks apiece. That says a lot about how Klanderman calls a game. He isn’t relying on one star pass rusher; six different players have at least two sacks, and he is willing to bring pressure from anywhere on the field, including the secondary. 6. What’s an aspect of this Bears team’s game that is not talked about enough? ​Haddadin: The most underrated part of this team might be the guy who comes on when the offense stalls. Senior punter Palmer Williams has quietly been one of the best weapons on the roster. He came into the year with plenty of credentials, as a 2025 All-American and Ray Guy Award finalist who earned first-team Walter Camp and second-team AP preseason All-American honors before this season. He picked up right where he left off. In the opener against Auburn, he punted four times for 208 yards, a 52-yard average, and earned Ray Guy Award Punter of the Week honors for flipping field position and helping Baylor get back into a game it nearly stole at the end. A month into the season, he was averaging over 50 yards a punt and consistently pinning punts near the goal line. He was a massive part of the win against Colorado in Week 4. As the offense struggled to move the ball, Williams flipped the field and pinned the Buffs inside their own 10-yard line on multiple occasions. If Friday’s game against UCF turns into a cagey field-position battle, Baylor won’t mind, since it has one of the best punters in the country. Pete Fiutak Thu, October 29, 2026 at 2:02 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Here's the punchline – both Baylor and UCF are 4-3 overall and 2-2 in Big 12 play. On one side, Baylor lost on the road to Kansas in a 25-24 fight, and that was it. Head coach Dave Aranda was fired, defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman is the interim head man, and the team needs this win with a tough November coming up. However, win in Orlando, beat Iowa State at home, and boom – the Bears are bowl-eligible. UCF lost on the road to Houston and Oklahoma State, and then it changed the national landscape – and got Scott Frost his first huge win in his second round with the Knights – with a 39-31 victory over BYU. With a very favorable finishing kick, UCF has to keep the momentum going. Baylor vs UCF: Quick Hits Baylor has the home date against Iowa State next, and then there's a problem – at BYU, Texas Tech, at Houston. UCF goes to Kansas after this, and then plays Arizona State, Iowa State, and goes to Colorado. None of those four are likely to go to a bowl game. It's the fourth meeting between the two. Baylor won 30-3 last year and won 36-35 in 2023, but UCF won a wild 52-42 Fiesta Bowl to end the 2013 season. How To Watch Baylor vs UCF Date: Friday, October 30, 2026 Game Time: 7:30 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando, FL – Week 9 Schedule, Game Previews – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predicting the First CFP Top 25 – CFN Week 9 Expert Picks Why Baylor Will Win The defense is taking the ball away in bunches. The run defense has been fantastic – Kansas ripped it up last week, but that was an anomaly – but the takeaways have been the biggest help, with 13 overall and at least two in four games. UCF doesn't have to get the running game going to win, but it's a huge help going 4-1 when running for more than 100 yards. Baylor has held four teams to under 100, but … Why UCF Will Win UCF isn't having a problem with turnovers. It has only given it up seven times, didn't turn it over against BYU, and it's +5 overall in turnover margin. So really, how did UCF beat BYU? The running game was effective enough – even if it wasn't dominant – and the passing game was fearless, and that's how the Knights have to play. They don't have to bomb away, but they should take the midrange plays against a Baylor pass defense that can get to the quarterback but is susceptible to quick hits. Baylor vs UCF Prediction, Betting Lines UCF needs to capitalize on the momentum, and it will. The Knights are 4-0 in the Bounce House, and 0-3 away from it. Baylor hung 55 at Arizona State and suffered two one-point losses away from Waco, but now it has to deal with the coaching drama and all the changes. The team will play hard and well for Klanderman, but the UCF offense will be just a bit more effective.
